main_body: A 4x3 block of riveted blue-grey metal floor/wall panels with dark gutters between them, including one panel variant with a cyan light and one with a recessed slot
top_band: Not a standing object. Columns x=16 and x=32 run through the dark gutter (L=50 for all rows 0-47). Column x=47 only crosses the gutter and a few rivet pixels, so there is no top band to read.
evidence: The kind is terrain: a repeating tile block of panel surfaces, not a standing volume. The 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply to it. Each panel has a lighter upper strip and a darker lower strip, which reads as a bevelled floor or wall plate. No receding side faces are drawn. The column scans give no standing-object structure to fail, so this passes as terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has 9 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 7 and 7 for the paving reference. It is only slightly lower on the per-tile median, and it has more distinct colours than the paving. It is well below the grass on both measures, but the paving is the closer reference for a panel floor. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines carry a blue-slate tint rather than a black sticker line. Panels have a highlight strip, mid, dark lower band, rivets, speckle dots and gutter shadow, so shading is about 5 steps. It is simple but not flat, and it holds up next to the paving reference.
